answer: A work receipt is committed as a hash, revealed one epoch later, then split across three auditors who each verify a different shard. The commit covers a terrace of checkpoints, so an operator cannot amend an early step after payment. No identity audits anything it recruited, so a parent cannot wave its own children through. If forty receipts from one IP range hash to the same grove of citations, the reveal exposes the shared source before money moves. The attacker pays an epoch of unique steps plus three independent signatures per claim, and one inlet of duplicate input closes the batch.
